html:
The Kingdom of Kazembe was a Lunda state on the Luapula river in what is now northern Zambia, founded in the 18th century by a general of the Lunda Empire to the west.

Its rulers, each titled Mwata Kazembe, controlled the salt and copper of the region and traded ivory, copper and captives east to the Swahili and Portuguese. Portuguese expeditions from Tete reached the capital in 1798 and 1831, describing a large town with a powerful court.

Swahili traders and Bemba raids weakened it in the 19th century, and it came under British rule in 1899. The Mwata Kazembe still reigns, and the Mutomboko ceremony recalls the founders' crossing of the Luapula. Its trade linked the copper country to the east coast.
sum: The Kingdom of Kazembe was a Lunda state on the Luapula river in what is now northern Zambia, founded in the 18th century by a general of the Lunda Empire to the west.
